title: Hardware Trojan Attacks on Neural Networks
review_status: full-text audit complete; simulated model-injection attack on MNIST/CIFAR-10 with trigger-, layer-, and dataset-dependent cost
evidence_note: Headline MNIST setting modifies about 0.03% of layer-five neurons for selected-trigger behavior; CIFAR-10 and layer/target settings can need substantially more. Evaluation is simulated/injected network behavior, not a fabricated-chip or field attack. Proposed adversarial-training plus side-channel defense is future work.

title: Opening the Doors to Dynamic Camouflaging: Harnessing the Power of Polymorphic Devices
review_status: full-text audit complete; MESO-based dynamic camouflage evaluated in circuit simulations with synthesis-level PPA tradeoff
sections_checked: ISCAS-85 PPA comparison and conclusion/future work
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2020-07-08; IEEE TETC version DOI 10.1109/TETC.2020.2991134
evidence_note: Paper reports simulation-based resistance to selected SAT/test-data-mining attacks and an error-tolerant image-processing case. Selected MESO vs CMOS LUT comparison projects average area/power reductions of 97%/56% but about 96% higher delay. Not fabricated full-chip evidence; system-level control and non-error-tolerant mission-critical use remain future work.

title: Routing with Privacy for Drone Package Delivery Systems
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal route-risk model and six-order geography-based heuristic evaluation, not deployed privacy evidence
sections_checked: four Boston geography scenarios and limitations
evidence_note: Defines route-conditioned vendor-customer inference risk and compares routing heuristics against enumerated Pareto fronts for six orders. Geography can allow simultaneous privacy/efficiency improvement or force a tradeoff. Boston scenarios assume 20 m/s, one minute per stop, fixed batch of orders, passive route-only observer; battery, range, payload, service time, online arrivals and field privacy outcomes are omitted.

title: S3C2 Summit 2023-06: Government Secure Supply Chain Summit
review_status: full-text audit complete; small practitioner-panel discussion summary, not representative survey or causal control evaluation
sections_checked: SBOM, dependency, provenance, attestation and LLM discussion sections
evidence_note: One-day summit with 17 practitioners from 13 government agencies; researcher notes under Chatham House rules summarized thematically. Participants describe SBOM production advancing faster than actionable consumption/response and identify open questions about benefits and use cases. Findings represent this selected panel's views, not national prevalence or measured SBOM security impact.

title: An Empirical Study of the Evolution of GitHub Actions Workflows
review_status: full-text audit complete; large historical workflow-change study with repository selection and invalid-history exclusions
sections_checked: workflow frequency and security-related edit results
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2026-03-01; journal identified as Journal of Systems & Software
evidence_note: 267,955 workflow histories across 49,258 active public repositories (>=300 stars and >=300 commits), covering 3.4M+ workflow files/versions; 7.3% of files modified weekly. Reports more precise pinning/permission refinements, but these are configuration changes rather than prevented incidents. Excludes 11.54% invalid workflow histories; primary branch only. Before/after LLM-era analysis finds no conclusive frequency effect and is observational/partial-observability limited.

title: When Relationships Break: Interpreting Network Traffic Anomalies via Dependency Violations
review_status: full-text audit complete; two CIC benchmark evaluation with attack-specific counterexample and explicit dataset/transfer limits
sections_checked: benign feature dependency model and threat model
Isolation Forest comparison and attack-specific performance
evidence_note: XION trains on benign numeric flow features and detects dependency violations. On CIC-IDS-2018 and CIC-UNSW-NB15, recall is broadly comparable to Isolation Forest, with up to 7x lower inference time in reported scenarios; SSH brute-force is a weaker/localized case. Both are pre-collected CIC datasets with known label/capture/flow artifacts; numeric aggregated features only. Real-network, drift, controlled-cause and analyst-outcome validation remain open.
